The majority of JET-ILW Hybrid pulses have core n=1 activity, while n=2 and n=3 activity is more common in JET-C.
The average maximum normalized pressure (βN) is 2.44 in JET-ILW and 3.03 in JET-C Hybrid pulses.

In JET-C, n=2 modes lead to a modest 12% reduction in confinement, while in JET-ILW the n=2 modes can rapidly accelerate on-axis peaking of tungsten impurities, leading to much larger confinement degradation.
Sawteeth are beneficial in the JET-ILW in flushing out core impurities, while fishbones inhibit core impurity peaking.
The n=2 island is generally located close to the q=3/2 surface, indicating an m=3, n=2 tearing mode.
At the highest βN (>~3), the m=3, n=2 neoclassical tearing modes (NTMs) are intrinsically unstable, whereas at lower βN they are often sawtooth triggered.
The tungsten impurity density tends to be radially localized just outside the radius at which the n=2 island forms, when the tungsten is still off-axis.
As the n=1 mode parity changes from kink to tearing, there is no discernible effect on impurity peaking, but the impurity peaking is likely assisted by the reduction in central temperature gradients.
Long duration (>3s at βN>3) high performance JET-C Hybrid pulses have not been achieved in the JET-ILW, largely due to constraints on the divertor power handling.
The n=3 modes almost always occur concurrently with n=1 modes during JET-ILW operation, and such concurrent MHD activity has the most deleterious effect on confinement.

Modeling shows that the n=2 island can increase the inward diffusion of tungsten, or affect the background deuterium fuel ion profiles, leading to enhanced neoclassical and turbulent transport of the tungsten impurity.

Once the tungsten density starts to peak on-axis, its evolution can undergo a non-linear feedback, where the associated increase in radiation reduces temperature screening, further enhancing the impurity peaking.
The magnitude of the enhanced tungsten diffusion coefficient inside the n=2 island region is a key parameter in determining the rate of on-axis tungsten peaking in the modeling.
The modeling predicts significant increases in central tungsten peaking due to the effects of the n=2 island on the fuel ion profiles and transport.
The edge tungsten density boundary condition is a key parameter determining the absolute magnitude of the on-axis tungsten density in the modeling.
